newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - will jobs data throw a scare?.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - will jobs data throw a scare?.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were flat to slightly firmer early Thursday, buoyed by data showing a softer economy, though traders braced for Friday's crucial payrolls data, which could throw a post-Halloween scare.

In what is viewed by some traders as a possible early sign of Friday's unemployment data for October, jobless claims for the week ended October 26 rose 342,000, exceeding the previous week's revised gain of 319,000.
Payrolls, which are due out on Friday at 0830 EDT, are forecast at 212,000, down 40,000, according to a consensus survey of economists by Reuters.
The market also was hoping that the release of the Chicago October Purchasing Managers Survey on Thursday at 1000 EDT will suggest that the economy is trending down.
The consensus survey shows economists look for a reading of 54 percent, down from 56.3 percent the previous month. A level below 50 percent indicates the economy is contracting.

The sale of $592 million of bonds by New York Urban Development Corp on Wednesday left traders wondering how many bonds still were on dealers' shelves, and how much of the offering had yet to find a home with investors.

Joe Branca, the head of finance for the Urban Development Corp, said, "I would say most of most of our serial stuff went away, most of the intermediates went away, you probably have some overhang on the terms, but it should be put away by the time the deal closes."
The deal was repriced by PaineWebber, which raised yields in several maturities, lifting the top yield in 2026 to 5.88 percent from 5.86 percent.

Branca said that the repricing was due to the fairly aggressive scale for the retail presale period, which preceded the sale by one day, and which was not changed for the institutional sale until the next afternoon.

He added that by restructuring the agency's debt in its first sale on its own in 20 years, it saved three percent on a present value basis even though the deal extended the agency's maturities by 12 years.
Traders were looking ahead to Thursday's sale of $775 million worth of bonds by the New York State Dormitory Authority.
The competitive calender includes almost $80 million of Mississippi general obligation bonds, which are due at 1100 EDT.

The December municipal bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade gained seven ticks to 115-15/32, slightly outpacing the December Treasury bond futures, which edged up three ticks to 112-22/32. This left the MOB spread at 89 ticks, down sharply from last week's levels.
Actively quoted issues included Cook County Illinois Refunding Capital Improvement issues of November 2022, which pay a 5-7/8 percent coupon, and which were bid at 99-1/2, unchanged.
Intermountain Power Agency Utah Supply Revenue Refundings of July 2021, which have a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.79 percent, down three basis points.
